member.name: T:geoDC.UiDriver.AutomationAudit
member.summary: Checks walked UIA snapshots against the AutomationId conventions in .

remarks.para: The rules, in the order findings are reported:

list.item: missing-id: an interactable node (see ) with no AutomationId. Data-bound items and everything inside them are exempt, because they are addressed by Name.

id-naming: an AutomationId that is not PascalCase {Noun}{Role} with a role from . One finding per distinct id. Toolkit template x:Names () and WPF's own PART_* parts are exempt from this rule and the next.
duplicate-id: an AutomationId carried by more than one node in the same page scope, other than a template part from . One finding per id and scope.
reserved-id: a reserved shell id from anywhere but directly in a top-level window, outside every page scope; a second such occurrence is reported too.
raw-name: a UIA Name that is unformatted ToString output, either record-style (Foo { Bar = 1 }) or a namespace-qualified type name (geoDC.App.FooViewModel). One finding per distinct type name.

remarks.para: A page scope is the nearest ancestor that accepts (an id ending in Page, a popup frame, a window, or a data-bound item), else the audit root. A node's own id belongs to the scope it sits in, not to the scope it starts. Within a rule, findings follow the document order of the node each one is anchored on (the first occurrence for a grouped finding), so the same tree always yields the same list. A node reached through two roots (same runtime id) is audited once, and the walk skips subtrees.

A parsed do invocation: the target and the steps to run against one shared session. Steps come either inline, as verb/option groups separated by ++, or from a script file (--file), never both.
A script holds one step per line, in the same grammar as an inline step. Blank lines and lines whose first non-blank character is # are skipped. Tokens split on whitespace, and single or double quotes group a token that contains spaces. Nothing inside quotes is escaped, so a regex keeps its backslashes ('^\d+ m$'). Inside single quotes, '' is a literal quote.
${name} is replaced by the value of --var name=value. An undefined variable fails the parse instead of running a step with a hole in it, and so does a --var the script never uses. Two directives may come before the first step. @target app|sample says which target the script was written for, so running it against the other one fails before any step runs. @var name=value gives a variable a default that --var overrides. Its value is the rest of the line, unquoted.
A run <script> [name=value ...] step, inline or in a script, is replaced by the called script's steps when the invocation is parsed. A script that cannot be read or parsed therefore fails the invocation before any step runs.
<script> resolves against , except when it starts with ./ or ../, already starts with , or is rooted. A ./ or ../ path is relative to the calling script's folder, or to the for an inline step. .ui is added when the name has no extension. The resolved path is read relative to the driver home.
The called script sees only the variables its run passes and its own @var defaults. The parse fails when a run passes a variable the script never uses, when the script's @target differs from the invocation's, or when a script runs itself, directly or through others.

member.name: T:geoDC.UiDriver.ScreenshotGeometry
member.summary: Coordinate arithmetic for screenshot, free of UI Automation and GDI so it is unit-testable on any host.
member.remarks: Four pixel spaces meet here. UIA bounds and GetWindowRect are physical screen pixels (the UI driver is per-monitor DPI aware). Window-relative physical pixels subtract the window's top-left corner. Surface pixels are the window's PrintWindow backing surface, which equals physical pixels for a per-monitor-aware window and is smaller by windowDpi / monitorDpi otherwise. Output pixels are the cropped surface after any --max-width downscale. Device-independent pixels (DIPs, 1/96 inch) are converted with the monitor's effective DPI, which is what a DIP of the app occupies on screen regardless of the app's own DPI awareness.

What changed between two readings of the same tree: the subtrees added and removed, and the nodes whose fields changed.
Nodes are matched level by level, among the children of a matched parent (or among the roots). A child with an AutomationId matches the child of the other snapshot with the same AutomationId. A child without one matches by control type and Name. When several siblings share an AutomationId, or a control type and Name, they match in order of occurrence. Children without an AutomationId that are still unmatched then pair up by control type, in order, when both snapshots have the same number of them left of that type. This step reports a text block whose Name changed as a name change instead of a removal and an addition.
An unmatched node is reported once, as the root of an added or removed subtree, and its descendants are not listed. A node whose parent did not match is not reported on its own, so a node that moves to another parent appears inside a removed and an added subtree.
